title: Mohawk Airlines 411
summary: Mohawk Airlines Flight 411, a Fairchild Hiller FH-227 turboprop, departed Albany at 20:03 EST bound for Glens Falls with 11 passengers and 3 crew. At 20:20 EST, while executing a VOR approach, the aircraft hit trees on the northwest slope of Pilot Knob Mountain at low altitude, impacted a rock cliff, and fell 34 feet before becoming lodged in trees and catching fire. The NTSB concluded the crew executed an improper instrument approach using an unauthorized modified VOR/DME procedure instead of the only legally available VOR 1 approach, combined with a severe downdraft.
probable_cause: The captain's improper execution of an instrument approach, combined with a severe downdraft at low altitude, resulted in uncontrolled descent into terrain.

factors.evidence: crew selected an improvised and unauthorized modified version of the VOR/DME 19 approach instead of VOR 1 approach
aircraft descended below safe altitude while in severe turbulence
severe downdraft at a low altitude
aircraft hit trees on the northwest slope of the Pilot Knob Mountain then impacted a rock cliff

events.text: Flight 411 cleared for VOR approach to runway 19 without ATC specifying which specific VOR approach procedure
Crew overflew Glens Falls airport and proceeded northbound, performing unauthorized approach
Aircraft hit trees on northwest slope of Pilot Knob Mountain, impacted rock cliff and fell 34 feet, caught fire
All 14 occupants killed; Flight Data Recorder recovered intact but Cockpit Voice Recorder damaged in post-crash fire

notes: Report reviewed; no formally numbered recommendations found in main text
